speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, and now you are experiencing similar issues in your right knee along with pain during urination. Do you have a fever or chills, and have you noticed any redness or warmth around the affected joints?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your symptoms and history, I suspect reactive arthritis, so I will check for eye inflammation and skin changes. Do you have any redness or pain in your eyes, or any sores on your skin or genitals? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and STI Panel
